```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(mdatools)
library(tidyverse)
library(prospectr)
library(broom)
library(purrr)
library(pls)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
```

# load data
```{r}
ICPMS <- readRDS(file = "C:/Users/poopm/Thesis Writing/Github/LPW_FT-NIRS/RDS_dataframes/ICPMS_filtered_GOOD_USEME.RDS")

FTNIRS <- readRDS("C:/Users/poopm/Thesis Writing/Github/LPW_FT-NIRS/RDS_dataframes/combined_IBM_LPW_raw.RDS")
FTNIRS <- FTNIRS %>% filter(region != "LPW")# select only IBM specimensof combined dataframe

# apply savitzky golay 1,5,17 filter
speccols <- names(FTNIRS)[grepl("^\\d", names(FTNIRS))]
metacols <- setdiff(names(FTNIRS), speccols)
FTNIRS <- cbind(FTNIRS[,metacols],
             savitzkyGolay(as.matrix(FTNIRS[speccols]), m = 1, p = 3, w = 17)
             )
speccols <- names(FTNIRS)[grepl("^\\d", names(FTNIRS))] # reselect the FT-NIRS columns
```


# PCA of FT-NIRS
```{r}
# perform PCA on all FT-NIRS columns, store alongside specimen
pca_FTNIRS <- mdatools::pca(FTNIRS[speccols], center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
# pca dataframe with first 20 PC's
pca_df <- data.frame(specimen = FTNIRS$specimen, 
                     pca_FTNIRS$calres$scores[,1:20])
# clean up column names
colnames(pca_df)[2:21] <- paste0("PC", 1:20)
```

# find averages for each region of each otolith
```{r}
ICPMS_summary <- ICPMS %>% group_by(specimen,transect,oto_region) %>% 
summarize(
    across(Ca43:PbTotal_ppm, \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )
```

# LM models

```{r}
library(tidyr)
# This ignores the transect column and averages all cores, all middles, etc.
ICPMS_region_avg <- ICPMS %>%
  group_by(specimen, oto_region) %>%
  summarize(
    across(Ca43:PbTotal_ppm, \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

# 1. Define the elements you care about
elements_of_interest <- c(
  "Mg24_ppm", 
  "Mn55_ppm", 
  "Li7_ppm", 
  "Zn66_ppm", 
  "Sr88_ppm", 
  "Ba138_ppm"
)

# 2. Create the chemical summary (average transects)
ICPMS_region_avg <- ICPMS %>%
  group_by(specimen, oto_region) %>%
  summarize(
    # Use the new .fn syntax for across, it's cleaner
    across(all_of(elements_of_interest), 
           .fn = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

# 3. Pivot wider
ICPMS_wide_region <- ICPMS_region_avg %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = oto_region,
    values_from = all_of(elements_of_interest),
    names_sep = "_"
  )

# 3. Now join and run the CCA
cca_data <- inner_join(pca_df, ICPMS_wide_region, by = "specimen")

# Your X-set (the 20 PCs)
X_vars <- cca_data %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("PC"))

# Your Y-set (just the names of the 72+ chemical columns)
Y_names <- cca_data %>% 
  dplyr::select(-specimen, -starts_with("PC")) %>% 
  names()

# Get the names of the PC columns
pc_names <- names(X_vars)

# Create the formula string
formula_predictors <- paste(pc_names, collapse = " + ")

# This will run one model for each element and store it in a list
model_list <- lapply(Y_names, function(chem_name) {
  
  # Create the full formula, e.g., "Li7_ppm_core ~ PC1 + PC2 + ..."
  full_formula <- as.formula(paste(chem_name, "~", formula_predictors))
  
  # Run the linear model
  lm(full_formula, data = cca_data)
})

# Name the list elements for easy access
names(model_list) <- Y_names

# # Example: Look at the results for Li7_ppm_core
# summary(model_list$Li7_ppm_core)
# 


# Make sure you have broom installed (it's part of the tidyverse)
# install.packages("broom")

# 1. Apply glance() to every model and combine into one dataframe
# The .id = "element_region" creates a new column from the list names
model_summary_table <- map_dfr(model_list, glance, .id = "element_region")

# 2. Select the most useful columns and rename RSE (sigma)
final_summary <- model_summary_table %>%
  dplyr::select(element_region, r.squared, adj.r.squared, sigma, p.value) %>%
  rename(RSE = sigma)

# 3. Sort by the best models (e.g., highest Adjusted R-squared)
final_summary <- final_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(adj.r.squared))

# Now just print the top of this table to see your best-fitting models!
print(head(final_summary))
```

# PLS MODEL

```{r}
# i think I should scale this shit first?

# Your X and Y data from before (using the data frames, not matrices)
X_vars <- cca_data %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("PC"))
X_vars <- as.matrix(X_vars)
Y_vars <- cca_data %>% dplyr::select(-specimen, -starts_with("PC")) 
Y_vars <- scale(Y_vars)

# 1. Run the PLSR model
# We'll use 10 components (ncomp = 10) and cross-validation ("CV")
# The formula is Y ~ X
pls_model <- plsr(Y_vars ~ X_vars, ncomp = 10, validation = "CV")

# 2. Get the Y-loadings (elements)
y_loadings_df <- as.data.frame(Yloadings(pls_model)[, 1:2])
colnames(y_loadings_df) <- c("LV1", "LV2")
y_loadings_df$variable <- rownames(y_loadings_df)
y_loadings_df$type <- "Element (Y)"

# 3. Get the X-loadings (PCs)
x_loadings_df <- as.data.frame(loadings(pls_model)[, 1:2])
colnames(x_loadings_df) <- c("LV1", "LV2")
x_loadings_df$variable <- rownames(x_loadings_df)
x_loadings_df$type <- "PC (X)"

# 4. Combine them into one data frame
loadings_df <- rbind(x_loadings_df, y_loadings_df)

# 5. Create the biplot
ggplot(loadings_df, aes(x = LV1, y = LV2, label = variable, color = type)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text_repel(max.overlaps = 15) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "PLSR Loadings Biplot (LV1 vs LV2)",
    subtitle = "Variables near each other are positively correlated",
    x = "Latent Variable 1",
    y = "Latent Variable 2"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# install.packages("vegan")
library(vegan)
# Your X and Y data from before (using the data frames, not matrices)
X_vars <- cca_data %>% dplyr::select(starts_with("PC"))
Y_vars <- cca_data %>% dplyr::select(-specimen, -starts_with("PC")) 
# 1. Run the RDA
# The formula is Y ~ X, or "Chemistry explained by PCs"
rda_model <- rda(Y_vars ~ ., data = X_vars)

# 2. Plot the model
# "scaling = 2" makes the angles between arrows reflect their correlation
plot(rda_model, scaling = 2, main = "RDA Triplot")
```


# correlation heat map

```{r}
# install.packages("pheatmap")
library(pheatmap)

# 1. Calculate the correlation matrix between the two sets
cor_matrix <- cor(X_vars, Y_vars)

# 2. Create the heatmap
# We'll cluster the rows (PCs) and columns (elements)
# to group similar variables together.
pheatmap(
  cor_matrix,
  main = "Correlation Heatmap (PCs vs. Element-Regions)",
  fontsize_row = 8,
  fontsize_col = 6,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE
)
```

# RDA

```{r}
# install.packages("vegan")
library(vegan)

# 1. Create a scaled version of your Y variables
# scale() returns a matrix, which is what these functions want anyway
Y_vars_scaled <- scale(Y_vars)

# 2. Re-run your PLSR model with the scaled Y data
pls_model <- plsr(Y_vars_scaled ~ as.matrix(X_vars), ncomp = 10, validation = "CV")

# 3. Re-create your loadings_df (the rest of the plot code is the same)
y_loadings_df <- as.data.frame(Yloadings(pls_model)[, 1:2])
colnames(y_loadings_df) <- c("LV1", "LV2")
y_loadings_df$variable <- rownames(y_loadings_df)
y_loadings_df$type <- "Element (Y)"

x_loadings_df <- as.data.frame(loadings(pls_model)[, 1:2])
colnames(x_loadings_df) <- c("LV1", "LV2")
x_loadings_df$variable <- rownames(x_loadings_df)
x_loadings_df$type <- "PC (X)"

loadings_df <- rbind(x_loadings_df, y_loadings_df)

# 4. Re-run the plot
# The points will now be spread out, and the ggrepel warning should go away!
ggplot(loadings_df, aes(x = LV1, y = LV2, label = variable, color = type)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text_repel(max.overlaps = 15) + # You might not even need max.overlaps now
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "PLSR Loadings Biplot (Scaled Y-data)") +
  theme_minimal()

# 5. Re-run your RDA (it will also look correct now)
rda_model <- rda(Y_vars_scaled ~ ., data = X_vars)
plot(rda_model, scaling = 2, main = "RDA Triplot (Scaled Y-data)")
```
